laat_vaar.blok: Onder die boom by die hek
laat_vaar.voor: Sy het hom 'n bottel gegee om slym in op te hoes.
laat_vaar.na: Sy het hom 'n bottel gegee waarin hy slym moes ophoes.
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: The stranded 'in' before the split verb 'op te hoes' is wooden; a relative clause reads naturally and keeps the meaning.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'n Bottel om slym in op te hoes' is a standard Afrikaans om-te construction with its preposition after the object; the proposal is longer and adds an obligation ('moes') without fixing a real fault.

laat_vaar.blok: Onder die boom by die hek
laat_vaar.voor: en sy kos het op die bord bly staan
laat_vaar.na: en hy het sy kos op die bord laat staan
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Sy kos laat staan' is the usual idiom for leaving food uneaten and keeps the focus on Oom Frans.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Sy kos het op die bord bly staan' is natural, vivid Afrikaans in the story's voice; the proposal is an equally natural alternative, so it is a lateral move.

laat_vaar.blok: Onder die boom by die hek
laat_vaar.voor: hy word nou al nagte lank wakker
laat_vaar.na: hy word nou al baie nagte wakker
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Nagte lank wakker word' can read as lying awake for nights on end; 'baie nagte wakker word' clearly means waking up night after night.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Nou al nagte lank wakker word met 'n nat hemp' reads naturally as waking night after night (like 'al weke lank'), and with 'word wakker' it does not suggest lying awake; the swap is lateral.

laat_vaar.blok: Onder die boom by die hek
laat_vaar.voor: dit is tuberkulose, en almal noem dit TB
laat_vaar.na: dit is tuberkulose, wat almal TB noem
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: A relative clause ties the short name to the disease more smoothly than a loose second main clause inside reported speech.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: The plain coordinated clause is clear for a Grade 5 reader; 'wat almal TB noem' is no clearer and can briefly parse with 'wat' as subject, so it is not clearly better.

vlae.blok: Onder die boom by die hek
vlae.teks: Oom Frans maak fietse reg onder die boom langs sy hek. Palesa stap elke middag ná skool daar verby en gee die spanner aan.
vlae.rede: The story opens in the present tense and switches to the past from the third sentence on; this reads as habitual background and may be intended, so it is flagged rather than changed.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Onder die boom by die hek
laat_vaar_vorige.voor: toe oorgestap na Oom Frans se hek
laat_vaar_vorige.na: toe na Oom Frans se hek oorgestap
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: In standard written Afrikaans the prepositional phrase comes before the past participle at the end of the clause.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: Placing the directional phrase after the participle is natural Afrikaans in a story; the reordering is a lateral move.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Onder die boom by die hek
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'Swaar' suits hardship; for remembering, 'moeilik' is the natural word.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Dit was swaar om te onthou' is natural spoken Afrikaans in a story and carries the burden of months of medicine as well as the remembering; 'moeilik' narrows it to the remembering only and spends the story's voice.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Onder die boom by die hek
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'Loop' for a disease is loose and colloquial; 'versprei' says plainly how it spreads without changing the meaning.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Loop' is the ordinary Afrikaans idiom for how a disease passes from person to person, and the original reads well. This sentence carries the checked claim on how TB spreads, so a sideways word swap is not worth the risk.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Onder die boom by die hek
laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Die kliniek gaan wel elke hoes van twee weke of langer na.
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Die kliniek ondersoek wel elke hoes van twee weke of langer.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: A clinic 'ondersoek' a cough; 'nagaan' reads like checking a document, and the protected wording stays intact.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Nagaan' (check) and 'ondersoek' (examine) are not the same action: the swap changes what the clinic is said to do with a two-week cough, and 'nagaan' fits the next sentence, 'Hulle kyk liewer te vroeg as te laat'.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Onder die boom by die hek
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Ma het tot die einde geluister
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'Klaar geluister' is clipped spoken usage; 'tot die einde geluister' says more clearly that she heard the whole story first.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Klaar geluister' is natural Afrikaans and says exactly that she heard Palesa out first; the proposal is longer and only reads differently.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Onder die boom by die hek
laat_vaar_vorige.voor: en die hoes was nou al meer as twee weke daar
laat_vaar_vorige.na: en die hoes was toe al meer as twee weke daar
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: In past-tense narration by the narrator, 'toe al' marks the time of the story more cleanly than 'nou al'.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: Narrative 'nou al' in past-tense storytelling is idiomatic Afrikaans and carries the story's voice; 'toe al' is a lateral move.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Onder die boom by die hek
laat_vaar_vorige.voor: niemand het iets daarvan gedink nie
laat_vaar_vorige.na: niemand het veel daaraan gedink nie
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'Iets daarvan dink' echoes English 'think anything of it'; 'nie veel daaraan dink nie' is the natural Afrikaans idiom for not paying attention to something.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The original is idiomatic enough in the story's voice, and 'veel' softens 'iets' from nobody paying it any attention to nobody paying it much, so the meaning moves slightly for no clear gain.
